In [[knot theory]], the '''6<sub>2</sub> knot''' is one of three [[prime knot]]s with [[crossing number (knot theory)|crossing number]] six, the others being the [[Stevedore knot (mathematics)|stevedore knot]] and the [[63 knot|6<sub>3</sub> knot]].  This knot is sometimes referred to as the '''Miller Institute knot''',<ref>{{MathWorld|title=Miller Institute Knot|urlname=MillerInstituteKnot}}</ref> because it appears in the logo<ref>[http://millerinstitute.berkeley.edu Miller Institute - Home Page]</ref> of the [[Miller Institute]] for Basic Research in Science at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].

The 6<sub>2</sub> knot can be represented with the following [[parametric equation]]:<ref name="t523">{{cite journal | last1=Boocher | first1=Adam | last2=Daigle | first2=Jay | last3=Hoste | first3=Jim | last4=Zheng | first4=Wenjing | title=Sampling Lissajous and Fourier Knots | journal=Experimental Mathematics | volume=18 | issue=4 | date=2009 | issn=1058-6458 | doi=10.1080/10586458.2009.10129057 | pages=481–497 | url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10586458.2009.10129057 | access-date=2026-07-26| url-access=subscription }}</ref>

:<math>\begin{align}
  x &=  \cos(2\phi) \\
  y &=  \cos(7\phi + \pi/4) \\
  z &=  \cos(\phi + 1.9065) + \cos(7\phi + 5.01637)
\end{align}</math>

with <math>0\leq\phi\leq 2\pi</math>.

The 6<sub>2</sub> knot is [[invertible knot|invertible]] but not [[amphichiral knot|amphichiral]]. Its [[Alexander polynomial]] is

:<math>\Delta(t) = -t^2 + 3t -3 + 3t^{-1} - t^{-2}, \, </math>

its [[Alexander polynomial#Alexander.E2.80.93Conway polynomial|Conway polynomial]] is

:<math>\nabla(z) = -z^4 - z^2 + 1, \, </math>

and its [[Jones polynomial]] is

:<math>V(q) = q - 1 + 2q^{-1} - 2q^{-2} + 2q^{-3} - 2q^{-4} + q^{-5}. \, </math><ref>{{Knot Atlas|6_2}}</ref>

The 6<sub>2</sub> knot is a [[hyperbolic knot]], with its [[knot complement|complement]] having a [[Hyperbolic volume (knot)|volume]] of approximately 4.40083.
